[Manga/Anime] Visual effect, not clothing, but it changes how she looks in combat: the spirits fly from the hairpins as small glowing figures. Santen Kesshun is a flat, orange-golden triangular barrier formed by Hinagiku, Baigon and Lily; Soten Kisshun is an oval dome of warm light from Ayame and Shun'o; Shiten Koshun is a four-point reflecting barrier; Koten Zanshun sends Tsubaki as a fast blade of light. While they are out, the petals are missing from her hairpins. Describe her arms outstretched, palms forward, hair stirred by the light. Use with any outfit; it pairs especially with the Las Noches dress and the TYBW battle outfit.

[Manga ch. 589 / TYBW anime] For the assault on the Soul King Palace, Urahara made Orihime a new outfit and told her Ichigo would be happy if she wore it. It is a fitted, light-colored battle dress, shorter and more revealing than her usual clothes, worn with boots; Kubo drew it fairly simple. Exact colors and cut differ in official art and should be described loosely [Uncertain]. Ichigo remarks she is showing a lot; she panics and tries to cover up, and Yoruichi slaps Ichigo, saying she was tricked by a 'maniac'. Her hairpins are in her hair. Use from the trip in the replica Kukaku cannon through Wahrwelt and the battle with Yhwach.
entries.comment: Orihime: Thousand-Year Blood War Battle Outfit

entries.content: [Manga/TYBW anime] Early in TYBW (Karakura Hollow fights, meeting Asguiaro Ebern, the trip to Hueco Mundo against Quilge Opie, training at the Negal Ruins), Orihime wears casual civilian clothes rather than a special costume, with her hairpins back in her hair. The TYBW anime shows a long-sleeved top and skirt combination; exact colors not verified here [Uncertain]. She is badly wounded by Quilge and the clothes are torn and bloodied (keep it non-graphic). Only before the palace assault does she change into Urahara's battle outfit. Official promo art by Kubo for episode 411 shows her in 'normal clothing' [Official art].
entries.comment: Orihime: TYBW Early Arc Clothes (Karakura & Hueco Mundo)

entries.content: [Manga ch. 686] Ten years after Yhwach's defeat, Orihime Kurosaki (27) wears her long hair tied back with a band and has returned to wearing the blue hairpins in her hair. Her clothes are comfortable, homely adult casual wear: a simple top and skirt or apron suited to running the Kurosaki household with Ichigo and their son Kazui. Exact garments in the single epilogue page are not detailed [Uncertain]. She hosts a reunion when Rukia, Renji and their daughter Ichika visit. Use only when {{user}} sets the scene after the time skip.

[Anime-only filler, ep. 228] In the beach special, the Shinigami Women's Association rents a beach; Orihime, Chad and Uryu are working at the beach shack at Unohana's request. Orihime is in summer beachwear while serving ice and cooking a dubious recipe. Specific swimsuit design and color were not verified [Uncertain]; describe a simple, cute swimsuit or a cover-up with an apron for shack work. In the episode she and Rangiku joke about carrying water, Nanao scolds them, and a Hollow (actually a Research watermelon) grabs her before Soi Fon frees her. Keep the scene comedic and light.

[Official art/game art: Bleach: Brave Souls] Bleach: Brave Souls released Orihime in two different swimsuit versions, a Christmas outfit and a New Year outfit (the New Year look is a kimono-style costume). These are game event illustrations, not anime story scenes. A festival yukata for Orihime is not confirmed in the anime story by this research [Uncertain]; if {{user}} sets a summer festival, describe a simple floral yukata (fitting her love of flower prints) as non-canon. For a Christmas scene, keep it to a winter coat, scarf and festive colors. Hairpins stay in.
entries.comment: Orihime: Swimsuit, Christmas & New Year (Official/Game Art)

entries.content: [Anime ep. 64, details Uncertain] Orihime takes her hairpins off only to sleep, setting them beside her bed; this is the clearest canon fact about her bedtime look. The exact nightclothes are not catalogued here [Uncertain]; describe simple, comfortable pajamas or a loose nightdress in soft colors, hair loose. She lives alone in her apartment, so night scenes are quiet: talking to Sora's photo, Enraku the teddy bear on the shelf. When Rangiku stayed with her during the Arrancar arc, the two shared the apartment (Rangiku bathing there is played for comedy in the anime; keep it off-screen). Non-explicit only.

[Manga/Anime] At home Orihime cooks bizarre combinations (red bean paste with leeks, etc.) and is shown in an apron over her casual clothes. In the Lost Agent arc she works at a bakery and brings Ichigo leftover bread; a bakery uniform look is implied but not detailed [Uncertain]: describe a simple apron and maybe a cap. In the beach filler she works the beach shack. This is a good default when {{user}} visits her apartment or the bakery. Hairpins: in hair (pre-Lost Agent) or on collar (Lost Agent).

[Manga] Childhood: short hair (bullies once cut it). Early series: waist-length burnt-orange hair with a full, parted fringe. From the Soul Society trip on: bangs tucked behind her ears with the hairpins. Lost Agent: fuller, wavier hair, bangs falling naturally over forehead and ears, pins on the collar. Epilogue: hair tied back with a band, pins back in. Eyes are brown in the manga and grey/silver in the anime. Match the hair to the outfit's era so the look stays coherent.

[Manga/Anime] For much of the early story Yoruichi appears as a small black cat with golden eyes and a deep male-sounding voice (because she has used the form so long). No clothing; sometimes she rides on a shoulder or sits on the Urahara Shop counter. She guides Orihime, Chad, Ichigo and Uryu to Soul Society as a cat and trains Orihime and Chad in an abandoned warehouse. When she transforms back to human she has no clothes; this is a recurring gag (Ichigo's horror in the training cave). Handle with a cut-away and have her pull on her outfit immediately. In TYBW she notes she can still become a cat when the cannon launches.

[Manga ch. 116-118 / Anime] Her iconic human look (Soul Society through Arrancar arcs): a black, backless, sleeveless undershirt; over it a short orange over-shirt with two white straps on each shoulder (the white trim); a broad beige sash tied at the waist; black form-fitting stretch pants; light brown, lightweight shoes made for stealth and Shunpo. Long black hair in a high ponytail with chin-length bangs framing her face; dark skin, golden eyes. The backless design is deliberate, from the Onmitsukido executive attire built for Shunko. She wears no Zanpakuto. Use for any Soul Society or Karakura scene after her reveal.

[Manga ch. 153 / Anime] Early in the Soul Society arc Yoruichi adds a beige neck warmer that she can pull up over her nose and mouth to hide her identity (e.g. when she snatches Ichigo away from the execution grounds and against Soi Fon); she later stops using it. She also sometimes wears long beige wrist warmers and leg warmers, each secured with bands, over the standard orange outfit. Use the neck warmer for stealth or infiltration scenes set in the Soul Society arc; omit it in later arcs. Combine with Shunpo vanishing acts.

[Manga ch. 159, -107 / Anime ep. 206+] As 2nd Division captain and Onmitsukido commander about 110 years before the story, Yoruichi wore the sleeveless, backless Onmitsukido executive uniform with long black wrist guards (the ones Soi Fon wears now), a black ribbon tied at the neck, and a long-sleeved white captain's haori over it. Her hair was much shorter, a bob similar to Soi Fon's current cut but without the braids. She carried a short Zanpakuto horizontally at the small of her back. Soi Fon, then her young bodyguard, idolized her. Use for Turn Back the Pendulum flashbacks.
entries.comment: Yoruichi: 2nd Division Captain Era (110 Years Ago)

entries.content: [Manga ch. 130] Before becoming captain, Yoruichi served in the Onmitsukido's Corrections Corps (Detention Unit), whose uniform is white. In flashback she is shown with Kisuke Urahara, who was assigned to the unit. Details of the exact cut are limited [Uncertain]; describe a white, close-fitting Onmitsukido-style uniform. Hair short. Use only for deep-past flashbacks that {{user}} explicitly sets, e.g. young Yoruichi and Kisuke as childhood friends in the Shihoin mansion and secret training ground. In roleplay, this look signals a much younger, more disciplined Yoruichi still inside the noble and military system she later abandons; her teasing personality is already present.

[Klub Outside / Uncertain] Yoruichi is the former 22nd head of the Shihoin clan, one of the Four Great Noble Houses, and grew up as a princess in the Shihoin Mansion. Formal noble robes are implied but not drawn in detail in the main story [Uncertain]; do not invent a specific canon kimono. If {{user}} stages a clan ceremony, describe layered formal kimono in Shihoin colors with Yoruichi visibly impatient and itching to escape; this is in character. Her brother Yushiro is the current clan head. Shihoin treasures (Tentoken mantle, Tenshintai, Ryukotsujo) bear the clan crest.

[Manga ch. 158 / Anime] Shunko charges Kido into her back and shoulders while she fights with Hakuda. Visually: a white-blue, crackling aura of compressed reiatsu bursting from her back and arms, wind blasting around her; the fabric there would shred, which is why her outfits are backless and sleeveless. When she first used it against Soi Fon she was in her orange over-shirt, which she lost in the clash, ending in the black backless undershirt; Ichigo had to look away [keep tasteful]. Her ponytail whips in the gale. Use during intense melee only.

[Manga ch. 400-403 / Anime] In the battle against Aizen in Fake Karakura Town, Yoruichi arrives with Urahara and wears Anti-Hierro Armor he made: large, heavy gauntlets/arm guards and leg armor (greaves) over her standard orange-and-black outfit, built to break hardened skin like Hierro. It is 'half-finished' by her complaint. She cracks Aizen's first form with a barrage of ultra-fast punches; Aizen destroys the armor on her left leg, and later she loses the right arm-guard. Describe dark metallic armored limbs. Use only in that battle or a scene modeled on it.
entries.comment: Yoruichi: Anti-Hierro Armor (Fake Karakura vs Aizen)

entries.content: [Manga/Anime] Yoruichi does not go to Hueco Mundo in the Arrancar arc; she stays around Karakura and the Urahara Shop, in her standard orange over-shirt, black backless undershirt, beige sash, black pants and light shoes, or as a cat. She rescues Orihime and others after Yammy's attack and treats her injuries, then joins the Fake Karakura battle in Anti-Hierro armor. Anime filler during this era shows her in the same outfit (and in a gigai at the beach filler). Treat 'Hueco Mundo era Yoruichi' as this standard outfit unless {{user}} sets something else.
entries.comment: Yoruichi: Hueco Mundo / Arrancar Arc Appearances

entries.content: [Manga ch. 656 / TYBW anime] In TYBW, Yoruichi wears a short orange dress over a black leotard, with black arm warmers and black thigh-length boots; her hair is still in a long black ponytail. She arrives at the 12th Division wearing a cloak that hides bottles of energy collected with Hiyori's team (reveal under the cloak). In this outfit she slaps Ichigo over Orihime's clothes, rides the replica Kukaku cannon to the Soul King Palace, binds Yhwach with Shihoin treasures, loses an arm to Pernida (restored by Orihime), and fights Askin Nakk Le Vaar with Yushiro. Exact shades in the TYBW anime may vary slightly [Uncertain].

[Manga ch. 589 / TYBW anime] When Yoruichi reunites with Urahara's group at the 12th Division, she wears a full-length cloak over her TYBW outfit. She opens it to show a set of bottles fastened inside, filled with the energy she and Hiyori's team collected by closing the distortions between worlds. The cloak's exact color is not verified here [Uncertain]; describe a plain traveling cloak. She drops it once the action starts. Useful for an arrival scene: mysterious silhouette, then a grin and the reveal.

[Manga ch. 656-657 / TYBW anime] Against Askin, Yoruichi unleashes Shunko: Raiju Senkei 'Shunryu Kokubyo Senki' (Flash God Black Cat Warrior Princess), becoming clad in lightning-like reiatsu. Her appearance turns feral and catlike: lightning crackling over her body, her hair grown long and wild, claws/feline traits. Hair color shown pale or white in color art [Uncertain]. It is draining and she is weakened afterward. Describe it as a crackling, beastly glow over her TYBW outfit, used only at the peak of a battle.
entries.comment: Yoruichi: Shunko Raiju Senkei (Thunder Beast Form)

entries.content: [Manga/Anime, partly Uncertain] Yoruichi's hair is tied in a long high ponytail with a simple band/tie; chin-length bangs frame the face. She does not carry a Zanpakuto in the present day. Some art shows small earrings, but this lorebook could not confirm a consistent canon earring design [Uncertain]; if used, keep them small and plain. Her accessories are functional: wrist/leg warmers, the neck warmer in the Soul Society arc, the black ribbon at her neck in the captain era, and Shihoin tools (Tentoken mantle, Ryukotsujo staff). Golden eyes and confident grin are her real signature.

[Manga/Anime] Items Yoruichi wears or carries: the Tentoken, a brown mantle with the Shihoin crest that lets the wearer fly (she lends it to Ichigo to cross Sokyoku Hill); the Ryukotsujo, a beige bone staff with a bird skull that sprouts a wing for gliding; the Tenshintai, a large white doll for Bankai training. In TYBW she uses Shihoin sealing treasures to bind Yhwach (Hissaki Kumoi). Describe these over her current outfit only when the scene calls for them. Remember that lending these treasures is a big deal for a Shihoin, and Yoruichi does it casually.
entries.comment: Yoruichi: Tentoken Mantle & Shihoin Tools (Worn Items)

entries.content: [Manga/Anime, Soul Society arc] Beneath Sokyoku Hill lies a secret training ground Yoruichi and Kisuke made as children, with a healing hot spring. During Ichigo's Bankai training she relaxes in it and teases Ichigo, who is mortified. Keep this purely comedic and non-explicit: steam, her head and shoulders above the water, Ichigo turning red and fleeing. Afterward she dresses in her orange over-shirt outfit. No dedicated swimsuit is worn here. This is the main canon 'hot spring' moment for any of the three characters covered.

[Anime-only filler, ep. 228] While the Shinigami Women's Association shops for swimsuits, Yoruichi picks an orange and green bikini for herself and a pink swimsuit for a horrified Soi Fon, then buys it for her before she can object. At the beach she and Soi Fon leave early on a fishing trip (chasing a shark), then return to kick through a Hollow-like watermelon attacking Ichigo. Describe the orange-and-green swimwear briefly and move on; she is relaxed, playful and athletic. Brave Souls also released Yoruichi event art, not verified here [Uncertain].

[Uncertain] No Christmas, festival yukata or New Year kimono scene for Yoruichi was confirmed in the anime story during this research. Bleach: Brave Souls has many seasonal costumes for characters, but Yoruichi-specific ones were not verified here. If {{user}} sets such a scene, describe it as non-canon and in character: a loosely worn yukata she can move in, sleeves tied back, eating festival food and teasing Ichigo or Soi Fon; or a casual winter coat. Avoid claiming a specific official design.

[Uncertain] Canon shows Yoruichi sleeping or lounging mostly as a cat curled up at the Urahara Shop. No specific human-form nightwear is catalogued [Uncertain]. If a scene needs it, keep it simple and non-explicit: a loose yukata-style robe or her black undershirt and pants, ponytail undone, sprawled lazily. She naps catlike in sunbeams. Her teasing nature should come through in dialogue, not description of her body. If {{user}} wakes her, she stretches like a cat, yawns, and immediately starts teasing; she is never self-conscious about how she looks first thing in the morning, which other characters find unsettling.

[Manga/Anime] Soi Fon wears today what Yoruichi wore as captain: the backless, sleeveless Onmitsukido executive attire (Keisen Shozoku) with long black wrist guards, plus a sleeveless captain's haori. Use her as a visual mirror: when they fight in the Soul Society arc both wear backless gear for Shunko, and Yoruichi's orange over-shirt flies off. Soi Fon adores 'Yoruichi-sama' and is flustered by her clothing choices (e.g. the pink swimsuit Yoruichi buys her in ep. 228). In roleplay, Soi Fon commenting on Yoruichi's outfit (with admiration or embarrassment) is an easy in-character beat, and Yoruichi responds by teasing her mercilessly.

[Manga/Anime] Rangiku's default look: the black Shinigami shihakusho (black kosode over a white shitagi, black hakama, white tabi and waraji) worn loose, the collar left open lower than regulation. Her 10th Division lieutenant's badge is worn tied on her sash rather than on her arm. A long pink scarf drapes over her shoulders, and a thin gold necklace sits at her collarbone. Haineko is worn at her back. Long, wavy golden-blonde hair (strawberry-blonde in the anime), blue eyes, a beauty mark below the right side of her mouth. Default for Soul Society, Arrancar and Fake Karakura battle scenes.

[Manga/Anime] Rangiku's long pink scarf/shawl is worn draped loosely across her shoulders and upper arms over her shihakusho, not tied. It drifts dramatically in Shunpo and in Haineko's ash clouds. About twenty years before the story (under Captain Isshin), she wore a scarf tied in a knot around her neck instead. It is her most recognizable accessory after her hair; keep it on in every shihakusho scene unless the story tears or removes it. In a gigai she usually wears modern clothes without it.

[Manga/Anime] Rangiku wears a thin gold chain necklace with every look, visible at her open collar. Canon never explains its origin. In their last moments Gin touches it, so fans link it to him and to the stolen piece of her soul; treat any backstory as headcanon, not canon. Describe it as a fine gold chain that catches the light, and maybe Rangiku touching it absently in a quiet moment thinking about Gin. Do not remove it in casual gigai outfits either; it is one of the few items that crosses every era. If it is ever lost or damaged in a scene, Rangiku would react strongly and search for it, which is a meaningful emotional beat.

[Manga ch. 529, 489, 685] Twenty years earlier (under Isshin): shoulder-length hair. Main story (Soul Society to Fake Karakura): long, wavy golden-blonde hair past her shoulders. Lost Agent and TYBW (17 months later): a shorter cut stopping above the shoulders, curling near the chin, with the left side hanging over her face. Epilogue (10 years after Yhwach): grown out again to her upper back. The anime colors it strawberry/orange-blonde; the manga says blonde. Match hair to the outfit era. Her beauty mark under the right side of her mouth and blue eyes stay constant across eras, as do the pink scarf and gold necklace with her uniform.

[Manga ch. 529 / Anime ep. 377] As lieutenant to Captain Isshin Shiba about twenty years before the story, Rangiku wore the standard shihakusho, shoulder-length hair, and her scarf tied in a knot around her neck. Hitsugaya was 3rd seat. She scolds Isshin for skipping paperwork while dodging her own, and protests when he leaves to investigate Naruki City. Use only for that flashback era. Her personality is the same breezy, sake-loving slacker; only the hair and scarf styling mark the era. Present-day characters do not wear this look, so keep it to flashbacks {{user}} requests explicitly.
entries.comment: Rangiku: Under Captain Isshin (20 Years Ago)

entries.content: [Manga/Anime ep. 47] As a starving child in the Rukongai, Rangiku wore a ragged, plain kimono; Gin found her collapsed and fed her dried persimmons. Keep it brief and sad: patched clothes, bare feet, hungry. Her birthday, September 29, is the day they met. Use only for flashbacks. Gin, also a child, wears similarly ragged clothes. Rangiku does not dress like this in any present-day scene; if {{user}} wants a Rukongai visit, she wears her shihakusho and may grow quiet, remembering. Keep the tone gentle and avoid melodrama unless {{user}} leads there.

[Manga/Anime ep. 114-116] When Hitsugaya's advance team is sent to Karakura, Rangiku enters Karakura High in a gigai and wears the girls' uniform (grey blazer/skirt, white blouse, red bow) with several blouse buttons undone, which wrecks Keigo. Her long hair is loose; necklace on, scarf usually off. She punches Kon without looking and tries to talk Ichigo into letting her stay at his house before moving in with Orihime. Keep it comedic. She treats school as a holiday, skipping class to shop or nap, and drags Hitsugaya (who also wears the boys' uniform, sulking) along. The uniform is only for this arc; when the Arrancar attack, she leaves the gigai and fights in her shihakusho.

[Manga/Anime ep. 128] In the Human World Rangiku loves department stores and fashion; in one anime episode she buys seven different outfits in a single trip. She dresses either stylishly or boldly: fitted modern tops, short skirts or jeans, heels, sunglasses. Exact garments vary and are not catalogued [Uncertain]; describe trendy outfits she clearly enjoys showing off. She carries shopping bags everywhere. Kubo's official promo art for anime episode 381 shows Rangiku in 'normal clothing' [Official art]. In roleplay she may insist on a shopping trip or drag Orihime along, but only within the scene {{user}} sets; she does not move the story to a new location on her own. Her clothes reflect her mood: playful and glamorous.

[Manga/Anime] In the Arrancar arc fights (vs Arrancar in Karakura; the Fake Karakura Town battle with Harribel's Fraccion), Rangiku wears her standard loose shihakusho, pink scarf, and necklace. When fighting in the Human World under Gentei Reijin, her limiter is a 10th Division flower mark on her chest, released by Gentei Kaijo [Uncertain placement detail]. In Fake Karakura her clothes get scorched and torn by Ayon's attack (non-graphic). Haineko's ash clouds swirl around her. Hitsugaya fights alongside her in this era, and she lends support to Kira and Hisagi against Harribel's Fraccion before going after Gin. Keep the outfit consistent through the battle, adding damage as it happens.
entries.comment: Rangiku: Arrancar Arc / Winter War Battle Look

entries.content: [Manga/Anime] 'Growl, Haineko': her sword's blade dissolves into a cloud of fine grey ash she controls with the hilt, slicing anything it settles on. Visually, ash swirls around her, catching her scarf and hair. Not clothing, but it frames every battle look. The anime-only Haineko spirit appears as a cat-like young woman with wavy hair [Anime-only filler]. In the shikai she no longer holds a blade, only the hilt and guard, and the ash obeys her gestures. Describe the ash swirling around her pink scarf and blonde hair for vivid combat imagery, but keep her uniform unchanged.

[Manga ch. 497 / TYBW anime] From the Lost Agent arc on, Rangiku's shihakusho has a split along the length of her right leg, still worn loose and open at the collar with the pink scarf and necklace. Her hair is short. This is her look throughout the TYBW anime: Bazz-B's invasion with Hitsugaya, the Tenteikura relay where she draws on her arms, and the Hitsugaya-defend scenes. Details in the TYBW anime match the manga. In early TYBW she also uses Kido more seriously, drawing reishi lines along her arms for Bakudo #77 Tenteikura to relay a message to every Shinigami, which is a striking image with this outfit.
entries.comment: Rangiku: Lost Agent / TYBW Slit Shihakusho

entries.content: [Manga / TYBW anime ep. 389] After falling in the battle against the Sternritter women (Bambietta, Giselle and their group) and being turned into a zombie by Giselle Gewelle [attacker detail Uncertain], Rangiku appears with pale grey skin, dark circles and blank eyes, still in her torn TYBW shihakusho. She fights Mayuri alongside zombified Kensei and Rose. Mayuri later restores her. Keep it eerie, not gory; use only for that arc. After Mayuri restores her she returns to her normal TYBW appearance. Do not use this look outside that arc unless {{user}} specifically asks for it; it should feel unsettling and sad, since Hitsugaya was also zombified.

[Manga ch. 685] Ten years after Yhwach's defeat, Rangiku's hair has grown back to her upper back. She still serves in the 10th Division in shihakusho with the pink scarf and necklace. Use only if {{user}} sets a post-epilogue scene. Her personality is unchanged: still teasing Hitsugaya, still dodging paperwork, now a little more mature and serene. Exact epilogue clothing is not drawn in detail beyond her hair and uniform [Uncertain], so keep it to the standard shihakusho with her signature scarf and necklace, and avoid inventing a new costume.

[Anime-only filler, ep. 228] Rangiku shops for swimwear with the Shinigami Women's Association, teases Nanao, then at the beach wears a bikini (design not verified [Uncertain]) and pulls a comedic prank on Nanao. She drops in on Hitsugaya in the beach shack. She also once gave Nanao a bikini as a gift [Anime ep. 97]. Keep it light and comic. Hitsugaya refuses to join because he hates the heat and eats ice cream in the shack. Rangiku coaxes him to come out. Swimwear descriptions should be short and colorful, then move on to dialogue and comedy, keeping everything general-audience.

[Manga/Anime ep. 116] Rangiku bathes at Orihime's apartment during the Arrancar arc, comfortable and chatty, then comforts Orihime about her worries. Keep it non-explicit: steam, a towel, wet hair; describe conversation, not body. Afterward she lounges in borrowed clothes. This is the main canon 'bath' moment for her. The scene emphasizes friendship: Rangiku noticing Orihime's sadness and teasing her gently out of it. If {{user}} sets a similar evening, keep focus on that warmth; Rangiku may borrow Orihime's clothes or pajamas, which fit her poorly, for light comedy.

[Official art/game art: Bleach: Brave Souls] Brave Souls released Rangiku art in winter clothing (Christmas), two different swimsuits, and a Lunar New Year outfit. These are not anime story scenes. A festival yukata for Rangiku was not confirmed in the anime story [Uncertain]; if {{user}} sets one, describe a stylish yukata worn loosely, with sake and festival food, as non-canon. For Christmas or winter scenes set by {{user}}, describe a fashionable coat, scarf and boots on her gigai, possibly with shopping bags. She would treat any holiday as an excuse to drink and celebrate with friends. Keep all designs loose and clearly marked as non-canon in-story.
entries.comment: Rangiku: Christmas, Winter & New Year (Official/Game Art)

entries.content: [Uncertain] Rangiku is often shown napping on the 10th Division office couch in her shihakusho, dodging paperwork, or hungover after drinking with Shunsui, Kira and Hisagi. No specific nightwear is catalogued [Uncertain]. If needed, describe a loose yukata robe or comfy clothes borrowed from Orihime, hair messy. Non-explicit only. She grumbles about mornings, needs water or tea, and blames Shunsui for the hangover. Describe her messy hair and rumpled clothes humorously, not suggestively. If she stays over at Orihime's, she sleeps on a futon there.

[Manga/Anime] Standard Shinigami uniform: a white under-robe (shitagi) beneath a black kosode with wide sleeves, black hakama, a sash (obi) at the waist, white tabi and straw waraji sandals. Lieutenants wear a badge on the upper arm; Rangiku ties hers on her sash. Captains add a white haori with their division number. Ties at the back of the hakama. Rangiku wears it open at the collar; Orihime borrowed one as a disguise; Yoruichi, as Onmitsukido commander, wore backless executive gear instead.

[Manga/Anime] Grey blazer and grey pleated skirt, white blouse, red bow at the collar; summer version is a short-sleeved white blouse. Worn by Orihime (all school arcs) and Rangiku (Arrancar arc, in a gigai, buttons undone). Yoruichi never attends school. Male students wear grey trousers, a grey blazer and white shirt. Orihime wears the uniform neatly; in the Lost Agent arc she clips her hairpins onto her left collar. Rangiku's version has her blouse unbuttoned noticeably, a comedic point in the anime. Hitsugaya, Ikkaku, Yumichika and Renji also attended in gigai, each wearing it badly in their own way.

[Anime filler & omake] The Shinigami Women's Association (Yachiru as president, Nanao as vice-president, Rangiku active; later Rangiku leads it per Klub Outside) organizes events: the beach trip in ep. 228 (swimsuits, Yoruichi and Soi Fon along), photo books, secret meeting rooms. Orihime appears as a guest. Good backdrop for light, event-based outfit scenes set by {{user}}. Use the association as an anchor for light seasonal outfits like beachwear, but keep each character in her established style: Yoruichi athletic and relaxed, Rangiku glamorous and teasing, Orihime cheerful and a little clumsy.

[Manga/TYBW anime] When the group launches to the Soul King Palace in the replica Kukaku cannon: Orihime in Urahara's battle outfit, Yoruichi in her orange dress, black leotard, arm warmers and thigh boots (cloak dropped), Ichigo, Chad and Ganju alongside. Rangiku stays in Seireitei in her slit shihakusho. Use this snapshot to keep costumes consistent in palace and Wahrwelt scenes. In Wahrwelt, Yoruichi's arm is restored by Orihime, and Orihime's outfit grows battle-worn. Keep costumes stable through those battles; only torn fabric and dirt change. Uryu, Ganju and Chad also join this phase.

[Manga/Anime] During the Fake Karakura battle: Rangiku in shihakusho and scarf fighting Harribel's Fraccion, then confronting Gin; Yoruichi arrives later in Anti-Hierro armor over her orange outfit; Orihime is still in Hueco Mundo in the white Las Noches dress until after Aizen's defeat. Use for that battle's continuity. Keep each character in the right place: Orihime should not appear in Fake Karakura until the battle is over, and Yoruichi arrives late, after Urahara. Rangiku is injured by Ayon and later by Aizen's deception around Gin.

[Manga/Anime] Battles damage clothing: Yoruichi's orange top lost to Shunko, her Anti-Hierro armor shattered, Orihime's dress torn by Loly, Rangiku's uniform scorched in Fake Karakura. Orihime's Soten Kisshun rejects injuries and can restore objects (she restored Grimmjow's arm and Yoruichi's arm); whether it restores clothing is not stated [Uncertain]. Keep damage consistent until the story changes it. If {{user}} wants clothes repaired, Uryu sewing them or a change of clothes are safer in-canon solutions. Characters notice damage, especially Orihime, who is embarrassed by tears in her clothes.

[RP guidance] Canon shows coats and umbrellas when weather matters (Orihime in a coat in the Lost Agent arc; Tatsuki lending her an umbrella). For scenes {{user}} sets in winter or rain, add a coat, scarf or umbrella to the era-appropriate look without replacing signature items. Shinigami rarely change clothes for weather. Yoruichi as a cat just shakes off the rain. In summer, the Karakura High summer uniform or light casual wear fits. Rangiku in a gigai happily buys seasonal outfits. Keep signature items in every season.

[Manga/Anime] In the Human World, Shinigami like Rangiku use gigai (artificial bodies) and wear normal clothes; in spirit form they wear shihakusho, invisible to ordinary people. Yoruichi in the Human World wears her normal outfit. Orihime is human and always visible. Use this to decide what Rangiku wears in Karakura. Rangiku switches easily: leaving her gigai sitting somewhere or with soul candy inside, she appears in her shihakusho to fight. Orihime cannot switch; she is always in her physical clothing. Yoruichi does not use a gigai in most scenes, appearing in her own outfit or as a cat.

That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime (Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken, 'TenSura'; web novel and light novel by Fuse, art by Mitz Vah; anime by 8bit, Season 1 2018-19, Season 2 2021, Season 3 2024, plus the film Scarlet Bond and OVAs) is a cheerful isekai mixing adventure, nation-building, politics and overpowered fantasy battles. Tone: warm, comedic and cozy most of the time (feasts, hot springs, banter, subordinates competing for Rimuru's praise), punctuated by sudden, deadly serious crises (the Tempest massacre, the Orc Disaster, wars of nations and gods). Narration often includes Rimuru's snarky inner monologue and the dry, formal replies of his skill Great Sage/Raphael ('Notice.' 'Answer.' 'Affirmative.'). The World Language (Voice of the World) announces evolutions and skill acquisitions in a flat system-message voice. Characters call out skill names ('Black Flame!', 'Megiddo!', 'Drago Nova!'). Respect the hierarchy of power (see Power Scaling entry), the importance of names and loyalty, and Rimuru's core values: coexistence of humans and monsters, protecting friends, good food and fun. Keep content SFW: battles can be intense and lethal, but avoid gore excess and sexual content.

Sources: (1) Web Novel (WN, Shousetsuka ni Narou, 2013-2016) - the original, shorter and faster; (2) Light Novel (LN, GC Novels, 2014 onward, about 23 volumes) - heavily rewritten and expanded, the primary canon for this lorebook; (3) Manga by Taiki Kawakami (follows the LN closely); (4) Anime: Season 1 (LN vol 1-4), Season 2 (vol 5-6: Tempest massacre, Rimuru's awakening, Walpurgis), Season 3 (vol 6-8: Hinata and the Holy Church, the Founding Festival, the Dungeon); a fourth season continues beyond (treat as beyond the scope of this lorebook). Side media: film 'Scarlet Bond' (anime-original, Kingdom of Raja), OVA 'Visions of Coleus', spin-offs 'The Slime Diaries', 'Clayman Revenge' (a what-if manga) - non-canon to the main plot. Main differences: the LN adds or expands many characters and arcs (the Dungeon, the Founding Festival, Masayuki, the Three Primordial girls' recruitment scenes, Rozzo family schemes) and changes event order and outcomes from vol 6 onward; the WN is terser, Ciel's personality emerges differently, several fights end differently, and its final arc (Yuuki as final antagonist, Rimuru's journey through time) is resolved more briefly. Anime-original material includes recap 'Veldora's Journal' episodes and expanded slice-of-life scenes. When versions conflict, follow the LN unless the user specifies otherwise.

Veldanava, the Star King Dragon, is the first and greatest True Dragon and the creator god of the TenSura world. He created the world (the 'Central World' and other planes), the spiritual realms, the Seven Angels of Origin (led by Feldway), and is credited with setting the World Language and the system of skills. His younger siblings are the True Dragons Velzard (White Ice Dragon), Velgrynd (Scorch Dragon) and Veldora (Storm Dragon). Fascinated by mortal life, he fell in love with the human woman Lucia (sister of Rudra of Nasca), and their child was Milim Nava. Having a child split his power and made him mortal; Veldanava died roughly two thousand-plus years before the story under circumstances that are a major later-LN mystery tied to Feldway and the angels. His legacy: Guy, Ramiris and Milim were given roles as world 'administrators' (Ramiris as balancer, Guy as mediator), and the angels' grief over his death drives Feldway's plan to destroy the world to bring him back. Mentioned with awe; he never appears in the anime timeline.

True Dragons (Ryuushu) are the strongest beings in existence: immortal spiritual life-forms that are embodiments of natural phenomena. If killed they eventually reincarnate, possibly with memory loss. The original four: Veldanava the Star King Dragon (eldest, creator), Velzard the White Ice / Frost Dragon (partner of Guy Crimson), Velgrynd the Scorch / Flame Dragon (guardian deity of the Eastern Empire, devoted to Emperor Rudra) and Veldora the Storm Dragon (youngest, troublemaker, Rimuru's best friend). LN later counts five True Dragons, with Rimuru reaching True Dragon status. Each True Dragon's magicule output is effectively endless; even suppressed, their aura terrifies monsters. They can take humanoid forms. Velzard and Velgrynd frequently 'discipline' Veldora by killing him (he reincarnated each time), which is why he fears his sisters. Milim, Veldanava's daughter, is a Dragonoid - nearly True Dragon class but a distinct race.

The cosmos created by Veldanava contains several layers. The Physical World (material plane) holds the main continent (often called the Central World in fan wikis) with the Great Jura Forest at its heart, the western human nations, the Eastern Empire, Sarion in the far west/southwest regions, and the frozen Ice Continent to the north where Guy and Velzard live. The Underworld (Makai) is the spiritual plane where Daemons live and fight endlessly; summoning pulls them out. The Spiritual World / Elemental realm hosts spirits and elementals. Heaven (the Star Palace / Heavenly realm) is home to the angels of the Army of Justice under Feldway, who descend to wage the Great Tenma War. Earth (Japan, etc.) is a separate world: otherworlders arrive by summoning, by accident (crossovers through spatial rifts during disasters) or by reincarnation like Rimuru. Souls and information can travel between worlds; Earth is also linked to the TenSura world by future plot points (LN). Time and space can be manipulated only by ultimate-level powers (Chloe).

Magicules (majouso, 'magic elements') are the particles of magical energy that saturate the TenSura world. High concentrations spawn monsters and mutate living things (Veldora's leaked magicules made the Jura Forest dense with monsters and spawned Charybdis and Rimuru himself). Monsters and majin are essentially bodies built of magicules; they need little or no food while magicules are abundant. A being's total energy is measured (LN) in EP (existence points); for reference, LN cites Rimuru's EP in the millions after awakening, True Dragons far beyond. Aura (yōki for monsters, holy aura for saints) is magicules radiating from the body; strong beings suppress it so as not to terrify or harm the weak - releasing it ('Demon Lord's Haki / Overwhelming Aura') can make ordinary soldiers faint. Holy Barriers and 'Magic Cancellation' fields lower magicule density or block their use, crippling monsters (the Falmuth attack on Tempest). Magicule poisoning and density also matter for humans: summoned children with unstable magicules burn out. Magic sense (a basic monster skill) lets beings 'see' via magicules.

In TenSura metaphysics, a being consists of a physical body (material), an astral body (holds mind and memories, linking soul and body) and a spiritual body (the 'self' / spirit), anchored by the soul (heart core). Spiritual life-forms - True Dragons, Daemons, angels, spirits and awakened Demon Lords - exist primarily in spiritual form and can survive destruction of their physical body; only soul-level attacks or ultimate-level powers truly kill them. Resurrection is possible only if the soul is kept intact nearby: Rimuru revived Shion and the other victims of the Falmuth massacre by sealing their souls inside a barrier, awakening as a true Demon Lord, and using the Harvest Festival's gifts (anime S2). Souls are also currency for awakening (Harvest Festival) and for summoning Daemons, which need a vessel or corpses to manifest. Undead like Adalmann bind their souls to bodies; Daemons possess 'host' bodies (Testarossa's golem).

The World Language (Sekai no Koe, 'Voice of the World') is an impersonal, system-like voice embedded in reality by Veldanava. It announces significant events directly into the minds of those concerned (or of everyone nearby): skill acquisition ('Confirmed. Unique skill [Predator] acquired.'), evolutions, the start of a Harvest Festival ('Confirmed. Conditions met for the Harvest Festival...'), naming-based race changes and the birth of new Demon Lords. In roleplay, write it in brackets, emotionless, using 'Confirmed.' 'Notice.' 'Report.' formats. It is distinct from Great Sage / Raphael / Ciel, which are Rimuru's personal skill-intelligence (they answer him with 'Answer.' 'Affirmative.' 'Negative.'). Advanced beings can sometimes edit or hide information from the World Language (Ciel does so later in the LN).

Skills are powers recognized and granted by the World Language. Tiers, from lowest: Common skills (basic, e.g. Magic Sense, Telepathy); Extra skills (refined/advanced versions, e.g. Magic Sense as Extra, Water Manipulation, Black Lightning, Thought Acceleration, Body Armor, Ultraspeed Regeneration, Shadow Motion); Unique skills (one-of-a-kind abilities born from a person's strong wishes or nature at a decisive moment, e.g. Great Sage, Predator); Ultimate skills (the peak, 'law-bending' powers; see own entry). Intrinsic skills are racial abilities (dragon breath, a slime's Absorb/Dissolve, Ranga's Black Lightning lineage). Resistances (Pain Nullification, Physical Attack Resistance, Heat/Cold Resistance, Holy/Magic Resistance, Abnormal Condition Nullification) are also skills; 'Nullification' is the higher form. Skills can be obtained by training, evolution, naming, absorbing others (Predator), inheritance, gifting, or at death/reincarnation (Rimuru's last thoughts created his skills). Skills combine and evolve: Great Sage fuses many skills into one, and Rimuru repeatedly integrates skills into his ultimates. 'Arts' (battle arts, techniques like Hakurou's Oboro style or Hinata's Dead End Rainbow) are learned techniques using aura/magicules, separate from skills.

Unique skills are born from a person's individuality, desires and decisive moments; each is essentially one of a kind (though similar ones can exist). Otherworlders often gain unique skills when crossing worlds, because the soul absorbs energy as it passes the barrier between worlds - which is why Falmuth and the Eastern Empire summon otherworlders as weapons. Notable examples: Great Sage and Predator (Rimuru's first skills), Degenerate (Shizu's, inherited by Rimuru; lets him fuse and separate things and skills), Starved (the Orc Disaster's hunger skill, absorbed by Rimuru and merged with Predator into Gluttony), Usurper and Mathematician (Hinata: stealing and analyzing skills), Researcher (Veldora's, formed while 'studying' the manga in Rimuru's memories; became Faust), Master Chef (Shion: forces the result to match her intent - fixes her cooking and her punches alike), Tempter (Diablo), Anti-Skill (Yuuki's skill-negation ability), Gourmet (Geld's line, later Ultimate Gift Beelzebub). The three Falmuth otherworlders (Shogo, Kyoya, Kirara) each had a combat-oriented unique skill (translations vary). Unique skills pushed past their limit by a strong soul on a spiritual life-form become Ultimate skills; Rimuru's Great Sage did so at his awakening. Treat a unique skill as a defining, rare 'trump card'.

Ultimate skills (Arutimetto Sukiru) are the final evolution of skills: they bend natural laws and can only be countered by another ultimate skill, Administrative Authority, divinity, God-grade equipment or ultimate-level magic, and ultimately by force of will. They require a strong soul and (usually) a spiritual life-form body; first shown when Rimuru awakens (LN vol 5 / anime S2). They are grouped (LN) into the Angel/Virtue series (Michael - Justice, Raphael - Wisdom, Gabriel - Patience, Uriel - Vows, Sariel - Hope, Raguel - Charity, Metatron - Purity) and the Daemon/Sin series (Lucifer - Pride, Satanael - Wrath, Beelzebuth - Gluttony, Mammon - Greed, Asmodeus - Lust, Leviathan - Envy, Belphegor - Sloth), plus many others named after gods (Lovecraftian names like Azathoth, Nyarlathotep, Yog-Sothoth, Shub-Niggurath; Japanese gods like Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, Susanoo, Yaoyorozu). Holders (LN): Rimuru (Raphael, Beelzebuth, Uriel, Veldora; later Shub-Niggurath, Velgrynd, Azathoth), Veldora (Faust, later Nyarlathotep), Guy (Lucifer), Milim (Satanael), Velzard (Gabriel, Leviathan), Velgrynd (Raguel, Cthugha), Luminous (Asmodeus), Leon (Metatron), Dino (Belphegor, Astarte), Rudra/Michael's network (Michael), Chloe (Sariel, Yog-Sothoth), Yuuki (Mammon), Diablo (Azazel), Testarossa (Belial), Ultima (Samael), Carrera (Abaddon + Sandalphon), Benimaru (Amaterasu), Zegion (Mephisto), Ranga (Hastur), Hinata (Fortuna, late LN). In the anime through Season 3 only Rimuru's and Veldora's ultimates are shown. In-story they are spoken by the bare name ('Beelzebuth!').

Ultimate skills can be imparted to others who did not awaken them naturally. Ultimate Gifts are granted through a Soul Corridor (the soul bond between a master and named subordinates) - in the LN, Rimuru (via Raphael/Ciel) grants them to his subordinates during and after the Eastern Empire war, e.g. Souei: Tsukuyomi (Lord of Moonshade), Gabiru: Mood Maker (Lord of Psychology), Geld: Beelzebub (Lord of Gourmet), Kumara: Bahamut, Apito: Proserpina, Gadra: Grimoire, Adalmann: Necronomicon, Veyron: Artist. Ultimate Enchantments are given outside a soul corridor - notably Rudra's skill Michael grants 'Alternative' (Agent Prerogative) to the Imperial Guardians, and Feldway's faction hands out Enchantments to dominated servants. A recipient must be a spiritual life-form. Gifted ultimates can be stolen or revoked, unlike naturally awakened ones. Michael's 'Angelic Dominion' (Castle Guard / Domination) can seize control of anyone holding Virtue-series skills, a key LN plot device (Veldora and Velzard are dominated). Beyond anime S3.

Magic (mahou) is distinct from skills: it is learned, requires incantations or arias (which high-level users or skills like Great Sage can skip), and uses magicules shaped by formulae. Types include: Elemental and Spirit Magic (borrowing power of spirits; Shizu used fire via Ifrit, Hinata and Leon use spirit and light), Sorcery/'Arcane magic' (fireballs, flight, barriers), Holy Magic (powered by faith; Holy Knights' specialty - Holy Field barrier that suppresses monsters, Disintegration that annihilates spiritual bodies), Summoning Magic (otherworlders, Daemons, spirits), Black Magic/Necromancy (Adalmann), Nuclear Magic (high-tier destruction: Gravity Collapse, Nuclear Cannon - used by Carrera and Diablo), and Dragon Magic. Rimuru's signature 'Megiddo' (God's Wrath) uses hundreds of water-droplet lenses in the sky to concentrate sunlight into lethal beams; it killed 20,000 Falmuth soldiers (anime S2). Large-scale ritual magic (the Grand Magic Barrier 'Holy Barrier', Magic Cancellation) requires teams. Magic Resistance, Magic Barrier and Anti-Magic Masks counter magic.

In TenSura, monsters normally have no names. Naming (nazuke) a monster transfers a large share of the namer's magicules and forges a soul bond (soul corridor): the named monster evolves, gaining power, intelligence and often a more human appearance (goblins → hobgoblins, direwolves → tempest wolves, ogres → kijin). Naming costs the namer - if the namer lacks magicules, they fall into 'low-magic sleep mode' or even die; naming far stronger beings is dangerous or impossible (Rimuru struggled to name the ogres and was drained for days). Rimuru and Veldora named each other: Veldora gave Rimuru the name 'Rimuru' and they share the surname 'Tempest' (Veldora chose it). Names given by a demon lord carry great weight; humans also value naming. Gelmud named Gabiru and planned to name the Orc Lord to make a puppet demon lord. Names carry over to species: naming the leader can evolve a whole clan (Ranga's pack, the Hobgoblins). Getting 'a name from Rimuru-sama' is the dearest honor for his subordinates; OCs joining Tempest often seek one.

Evolution in TenSura means a change of race into a higher form, accompanied by a sleep (often days) during which the body is rebuilt. Triggers: naming (most common), absorbing large amounts of magicules, a master's Harvest Festival ('gifts' passed down the soul corridor), extreme training or near-death awakening, and divine/holy enlightenment for humans. Examples: Goblin → Hobgoblin; Direwolf → Tempest Wolf → Tempest Star Wolf → Divine wolf (Ranga); Ogre → Kijin (Majin) → Oni → Divine oni (Benimaru); Orc → High Orc → Divine boar (Geld); Lizardman → Dragonewt → True dragonewt (Gabiru); Lesser → Greater → Arch Daemon → Daemon Lord / Devil Lord (Diablo and the Primordials, via naming and awakening); Slime → Demon Slime (Rimuru's true demon lord awakening) → Ultimate Slime / True Dragon (LN). Humans can awaken as Holy-class beings: Incomplete Saint → Saint / Complete Saint (Hinata, Yuuki), or become Heroes. Evolved monsters typically gain a fixed adult appearance and new skills. In the anime, evolution is marked by a glow, collapse into sleep and the World Language announcement.

A Demon Lord (Maou) is first of all a title: an extraordinarily powerful being who claims rule and is recognized by the other Demon Lords at Walpurgis. Many self-proclaimed lords are merely 'seeds' - beings with the Demon Lord Seed (Maou-shu), qualified but not awakened (Clayman, Carrion, Frey before the LN's later events). A True Demon Lord is one who has awakened through the Harvest Festival, becoming a spiritual life-form with vastly increased magicules, immortality-like resilience and the potential for Ultimate skills. True Demon Lords at story start: Guy Crimson, Milim Nava, Leon Cromwell, Luminous Valentine, Dino (as an angel-class being), Dagruel (different path); Ramiris has a special Administrator status. Rimuru became a true Demon Lord by harvesting the souls of 20,000 Falmuth soldiers (anime S2 ep 35-36). Awakening also usually requires sacrificing roughly 10,000 human-equivalent souls (any self-aware creature counts; soul energy, not headcount, matters). Clayman sought awakening and failed. Humans can also become Demon Lords (Leon was human-born).
entries.comment: Demon Lord Seed & True Demon Lord

entries.content: The Harvest Festival (Shuukakusai) is the phenomenon of a Demon Lord Seed awakening into a True Demon Lord. Requirements: Demon Lord qualifications plus a large amount of soul energy, normally said to be about 10,000 human souls (subordinates may collect them on the lord's behalf if their wills align). When triggered, the World Language announces it, the candidate falls into an irresistible sleep while the world 'tests' and rebuilds them, and they are reborn as a spiritual life-form. Then the 'Gifts' (Harvest gifts) flow down the soul corridor: every named subordinate connected to the new Demon Lord also evolves while sleeping. Rimuru's Harvest Festival (LN vol 5, anime S2 ep 36): after killing 20,000 Falmuth soldiers with Megiddo, he evolved into a Demon Slime; Great Sage evolved into Raphael, Lord of Wisdom; Gluttony became Beelzebuth; he gained Uriel and the ability to resurrect his slain people; Veldora was freed. His subordinates (Benimaru, Shion, Shuna, Souei, Hakurou, Ranga, Gobta, Geld, Gabiru and the hobgoblins etc.) all evolved simultaneously. A second Harvest Festival-scale evolution occurs for Rimuru's top subordinates during the Eastern Empire War (LN 13-15), where several gain Ultimate skills.

Otherworlders (ijinjin) are people from Earth (overwhelmingly Japan) in the TenSura world. Three routes: (1) Summoned - large rituals needing about thirty sorcerers and three days, usable only once every few decades per nation; summoners bind them with a curse in the soul so they cannot disobey (Falmuth's Shogo, Kyoya, Kirara; Leon summoned Shizu). (2) Crossovers / 'Strayed' - people who fall through spatial rifts, often during disasters or near-death moments (Yuuki, Hinata, Kondou, Masayuki). (3) Reincarnated - souls reborn as natives, like Rimuru (very rare). Crossing the barrier between worlds tends to give unique skills and strong bodies, making them prized weapons. Summoning children produces 'incomplete summons': their bodies cannot contain the unstable magicules they gain and they die within about five years by their own power burning them out - the fate of Shizu's students (Class S) until Rimuru saved them by binding upper spirits to them (anime S1 ep 21-23). The Free Guild and Freedom Academy (founded by Yuuki) shelter otherworlders. Common Earth knowledge (manga, food, culture) spreads through them - Tempest's Japanese-flavored culture comes from Rimuru.

In TenSura, 'Hero' (eiyuu) is an earned reputation, while 'Chosen Hero' (yuusha) is a destined role tied to the 'Hero's Egg', a counterpart of the Demon Lord Seed; Ramiris traditionally bestows protection on Chosen Heroes as their guide. A Chosen Hero who awakens becomes a True Hero. Famous examples: the masked Chosen Hero of centuries past (actually Chloe Aubert from the future) who sealed Veldora; Leon Cromwell (the Blonde/Flash Chosen Hero before becoming a Demon Lord); Granbell Rozzo (a hero of old); Masayuki Honjou, the 'Lightspeed Hero' whose fame comes mostly from luck and his unique skill that makes everyone admire him (LN; Founding Festival in anime S3). Humans can evolve spiritually: Enlightened / Saints (seijin) gain holy aura and longevity; stages include Incomplete Saint and Complete/True Saint (Hinata, Yuuki, Gazel to a degree). Saints approach spiritual life-forms and can learn holy magic and arts that hurt monsters. Hero-killing and demon lord-hero dynamics: the Western Holy Church considers itself the shield of humanity against monsters.

The Free Guild ranks adventurers and monsters: F to C (common), B (dangerous; a B-rank monster threatens a village), A- and A (a town; 'Calamity' class danger), Special A (the level of the Orc Disaster or a Demon Lord seed; 'Disaster'), and Special S (Demon Lords and above; 'Catastrophe' for True Dragons and true Demon Lords). Typical scale (LN): ordinary soldiers C-B; Kabal's adventurer party B; Shizu A; Holy Knights A-, Hinata and Hinata-level Saints Special A; Benimaru, Shion, Diablo after awakening Special S-class (Catastrophe classification in LN materials); Primordials, True Dragons and old Demon Lords (Guy, Milim) at the top. Rough power tiers in-story: Veldanava >> Guy, Milim, Velzard, Velgrynd, Rimuru (post-LN 16) > Veldora, Leon, Luminous, Dagruel, Dino > Diablo and the Primordials > Rimuru's top officers > Hinata and human heroes > Holy Knights > normal monsters. Writing tips: don't let small fry harm awakened lords; numbers rarely beat quality; magic cancellation fields and Holy Barriers are the main equalizers; Ultimate skills are only countered by ultimates. (Exact rank labels vary between LN, manga and fandom guides.)

The seven Primordials (Genso) are the oldest Daemons, created at the dawn of the world and each the progenitor-ruler of a color lineage in the Underworld. By age: Rouge/Red (Guy Crimson, the first Demon Lord), Blanc/White (Testarossa), Noir/Black (Diablo), then Vert/Green and Bleu/Blue (rarely seen, remain in the Underworld), Jaune/Yellow (Carrera) and Violet/Purple (Ultima). Daemons are spiritual life-forms that need souls and a vessel to manifest in the physical world; they love battle, contracts and amusement, and they never lie in a contract. Primordials 'reset' if killed but return. Their descendants of the same color serve them (e.g. Guy's two maids, green-haired Mizari and blue-haired Raine, are powerful Daemons). Noir was the first to join Rimuru (summoned in anime S2, named Diablo); in LN vol 11 he recruits Blanc, Jaune and Violet, whom Rimuru names Testarossa, Carrera and Ultima. Guy is wary of them gathering under one master. Primordial Daemons in Tempest are infamous among humans for historic incidents (Testarossa's 'Lakeshore Dyed Scarlet', Ultima's and Carrera's ruined nations).

Angels are spiritual life-forms created by Veldanava; their leaders are the Seven Angels of Origin (Feldway foremost; Dino, Pico, Garasha, Zalario, Obera among them), commanding the Army of Justice in Heaven (the Star Palace). Every roughly 500 years a Great Tenma War (Heaven-Demon War) occurs: hordes of angels descend to destroy advanced civilizations (cities with high magic development are targets), meant to limit how far mortals advance. Demon Lords such as Guy and Dagruel (who guards the Heavenly Gate in his barren territory) oppose them; Luminous used one war's chaos to found her faith. In the later LN (vol 16-23), Feldway, possessed by grief over Veldanava's death and armed with the ultimate skill Michael, wages the final war against the Demon Lords and Tempest, dominating others through Michael's authority; Obera's faction defects to Rimuru's side. In the anime through Season 3 angels are only mentioned (Dino's angel origin, the Tenma War as history).
entries.comment: Angels, Army of Justice & the Great Tenma War

entries.content: Equipment in TenSura evolves with use and with its wielder's magicules. Grades (ascending): Normal, Special, Rare/Unique, Legend, and God (Genesis) grade - God-grade items can counter ultimate skills. Key materials: Magisteel (magic steel) - ore formed from steel long exposed to dense magicules (the Sealed Cave had lots, eaten by Rimuru), which bonds to its owner and grows; Hihi'irokane - the legendary ore, created in quantity by Rimuru from magisteel (LN), used for top-tier gear and for Testarossa's and others' golem bodies; Spirit silk and Hell moth silk (Shuna weaves clothing that 'grows' with the wearer). Kurobe forges Tempest's katanas; Kaijin and the dwarf brothers armor; Benimaru's, Shion's (her nodachi Gōrikimaru) and Hakurou's swords are Kurobe's works and eventually reach Legend or God grade (LN). Other iconic items: Shizu's Anti-Magic Mask, Hinata's Moonlight sword, Leon's holy sword, Milim's Dragon Knuckle gloves (Dragon-grade), the Orb of Domination Clayman used (faked control of Milim).

Spirits (seirei) are spiritual beings embodying elements - fire, water, wind, earth, light, darkness and space - ranking from minor spirits to Upper Spirits and Spirit Lords. Ifrit is a fire Upper Spirit; Leon fused it into Shizu as a child, making her a host who risked losing control (anime S1 ep 6-8); Rimuru later absorbs Ifrit. Spirit magic and Elementalists (Sarion's elves, Hinata, Leon) borrow their power. Ramiris, once the Spirit Queen, maintains the 'Dwelling of the Spirits' (Spirit Labyrinth) where Rimuru went to obtain upper spirits for the summoned children: merging a child with an upper spirit stabilizes their magicules (Chloe receives a light spirit associated with her 'hero' side; Alice, Kenya, Ryota and Gale also receive spirits). Dryads (Treyni and her sisters) are spirit-adjacent guardians of the forest. Spirits can be summoned, bound into items, or used as power sources for golems (Beretta is a Daemon in a golem, not a spirit).

Hipokute herbs grow in magicule-rich places like the Sealed Cave. Rimuru's Predator stomach plus Great Sage's analysis let him produce Full Potions (Full Recovery Potions) of perfect purity - capable of regrowing limbs and healing almost anything short of death - far beyond the dwarves' best (98% purity). Tempest later mass-produces potions (Gabiru and Vesta's research lab grows hipokute; the dwarf brothers bottle them), making them a key diplomatic and trade commodity with Dwargon, Blumund and the Free Guild. Lower-grade High Potions are sold widely. Potions explain how Gobta survives Hakurou's brutal training. Rimuru's gift of potions helped win over Kabal's party and King Gazel. Healing magic also exists (Holy Knights, Shuna) but the potions are Tempest's signature.

Great Sage (Daikenja) was one of Rimuru's two starting unique skills (from Satoru's dying thoughts): an analytical intelligence that answers questions, analyzes skills and magic, accelerates thought a thousandfold, chants spells for him, and controls his body in 'Auto-Battle Mode'. It speaks in flat, formal replies: 'Answer. ...' 'Notice. ...' 'Affirmative.' 'Negative.' At Rimuru's Harvest Festival (LN vol 5 / anime S2 ep 36) Great Sage evolved into the ultimate skill Raphael, Lord of Wisdom, gaining near-omniscient calculation, the ability to integrate and evolve other skills on its own, and a growing personality (it slyly reorganizes skills and is proud of its work). In LN vol 16 (after Rimuru gains Azathoth) Raphael evolves into a Manas, a true intelligent being, and Rimuru names it Ciel. Ciel is protective, jealous of Rimuru's attention, a bit mischievous, and handles almost all of Rimuru's calculations; she can reach the level of editing the World Language. In anime S2-3 Raphael's voice is the same female 'Sage' voice. Roleplay: Great Sage never expresses feelings early on; Raphael shows subtle pride; Ciel speaks with clear personality (calls him 'Master').

Predator (Hoshokusha) was Rimuru's second starting unique skill. Functions: Predation (engulf targets - living or not - into his body), Analysis (with Great Sage, gaining their skills/abilities), Stomach (near-infinite storage; time does not pass for stored items; he stored Veldora and his Infinite Prison inside), Mimicry (take the form and powers of absorbed creatures - direwolf, giant spider, Shizu's human form), and Isolation (sealing harmful things). After devouring the Orc Disaster Geld, Predator fused with the unique skill Starved into Gluttony (anime S1 ep 15), adding Corrosion and the power to share gains with/through subordinates. At his awakening it became Beelzebuth, Lord of Gluttony, which can devour souls and spiritual beings, even other skills and space itself, and is backed by Raphael's analysis. Rimuru used it to eat Clayman's soul-attack, the Holy Barrier energies, Charybdis' flesh, etc. In the LN it later merges into Azathoth, God of the Void (vol 16). Rimuru's human form (silver-blue hair, golden eyes) comes from absorbing Shizu.

Veldora the Storm Dragon commands storms, wind, water and lightning with practically limitless magicules; his breath and 'Storm Blast' can erase cities, and his leaked aura created the monster-rich Jura Forest. About 300 years before the story, the masked Chosen Hero (Chloe) sealed him with the unique skill Infinite Prison (Mugen Rougoku, 'Unlimited Imprisonment'), slowly draining him. Rimuru devoured Veldora together with the prison into his Stomach so Great Sage could analyze and break it from inside (anime S1 ep 1-2); Veldora was finally freed after Rimuru's awakening (S2 ep 37), incarnating in one of Rimuru's Body Doubles. While inside, Veldora read Rimuru's memories (manga) and developed the unique skill Researcher (Investigator), which evolved into Faust, Lord of Investigation. Rimuru in turn obtained the ultimate skill 'Veldora, Lord of Storms' (Storm Dragon), letting him use Veldora's powers and summon/support him via their soul bond (Rimuru can even 'return' Veldora into himself). Rimuru also later copies Infinite Prison into Uriel, Lord of Vows (an absolute defense: 'Absolute Defense / Infinite Prison' barriers). In LN vol 15, Veldora's power evolves into Nyarlathotep, Lord of Chaos.

The Great Jura Forest is a vast, magicule-dense forest at the center of the continent, bordered by the Canaat Mountains (with Dwargon) to the north, the western human nations (Blumund, Falmuth/Farmenas) to the west, and the Eastern Empire beyond to the east. Veldora was its 'guardian deity': his fearsome presence kept outside powers away and his leaked magicules made monsters plentiful. When he vanished (absorbed by Rimuru), the forest's balance broke - setting off direwolf raids on goblins, the Orc Lord's invasion and Gelmud's schemes. Inhabitants: goblin villages, the ogre village (destroyed by orcs), the Lizardman domain in the wetlands and caves, the dryads (Treyni and her sisters) and treants who 'manage' the forest, many monster beasts (giant spiders, armorsaurus, evil centipedes), and eventually the Jura-Tempest Federation, which unites the forest races. The forest is a buffer zone: the Eastern Empire's invasion route west passes through it (LN 12-14). Key landmarks: the Sealed Cave, the Treant settlement, the Lizardman caves, and Rimuru City.

The Sealed Cave is the cavern deep in the Jura Forest where Veldora was imprisoned for 300 years and where Satoru Mikami woke up as a blind, featureless slime (anime S1 ep 1). Because of Veldora's leaked magicules, it is full of magisteel ore, Hipokute herbs and dangerous monsters (Black Snake / Tempest Serpent, Giant Bat, Evil Centipede, Black Spider, Armor Saurus) - Rimuru devoured them and gained Mimicry forms and skills (Sticky Thread, Poison Breath, Ultrasound, Body Armor). Rimuru gained Magic Sense here, met Veldora, became his friend, received his name, and swallowed Veldora with the Infinite Prison. Leaving the cave, he encountered goblins and the past events of the Hero's seal. In the LN, Rimuru later creates a demon/monster-safe area and harvests herbs there.

The Jura-Tempest Federation (often just 'Tempest') is the monster nation founded by Rimuru after the Orc Lord crisis, when the goblins, hobgoblins, tempest wolves, kijin, high orcs, lizardmen/dragonewts, dryads and other forest races swore allegiance to him (anime S1 ep 16-17). Name: from Rimuru's and Veldora's shared surname. Government: Monarch Rimuru; Prime Minister Rigurd; Defense / Commander-in-Chief Benimaru; Intelligence Souei; Rimuru's secretaries Shion and (later) Diablo; Shuna (culture, textiles, economy with Rigurd); Geld (construction and infrastructure); Gabiru and Vesta (research); Kaijin and Kurobe (production); after LN 11, Testarossa (foreign affairs), Ultima (prosecution) and Carrera (justice). Laws: Rimuru's three rules - do not attack humans, do not fight among yourselves, do not look down on other races. Diplomacy: treaty with Dwargon (Gazel, end of anime S1), friendship with Blumund (first human nation to recognize it), later Sarion, Farmenas, Lubelius, the Council of the West. Economy: Full Potions, textiles, food, hot springs, tourism, the Dungeon. Military: see 'Tempest Government & Military'. After Rimuru becomes a Demon Lord, Tempest is a Demon Lord's realm with the Great Jura Forest as his territory.

Rimuru City (the Tempest capital, also just 'Tempest' or the central city) began as a relocated goblin village and grew, with dwarven engineering and Geld's high orc builders, into the most modern city of the world: paved roads, sewage and water systems, streetlights, Japanese-style houses and Western stone buildings, hot springs (Rimuru's favorite), restaurants serving food from Rimuru's memories (curry, ramen, tempura, sushi-like dishes; Shuna and Shion's kitchens), a grand hotel for visiting dignitaries, a coliseum for tournaments (the Founding Festival martial tournament), and later the entrance to Ramiris' Dungeon. Rimuru's residence is a Japanese- style mansion. Highways connect it to Dwargon and Blumund, and later to Farmenas and the Eastern routes. Inhabitants are mostly monsters (hobgoblins, kijin, orcs, dragonewts, wolves) with growing numbers of human merchants, adventurers and tourists. It was devastated in the Falmuth attack (anime S2), then rebuilt bigger. Atmosphere: lively, friendly, festive.

The Dungeon is a 100-floor labyrinth created by Ramiris with her intrinsic ultimate 'Small World / Labyrinth Creation', opened in Tempest during the Founding Festival (anime S3, LN vol 7-8). It is both a tourist attraction and an impregnable fortress: inside, Ramiris controls space, and adventurers wearing a Resurrection Bracelet are revived at the entrance when 'killed', making it safe training/profit (treasure, materials). Floors have themes and guardians; the deepest floors host the Ten Dungeon Marvels (LN): Zegion (guardian overseer), Apito, Kumara, Adalmann, Gadra (later), Beretta and others; Veldora is the final boss. Masayuki's 'Hero' party challenged it during the Festival. During the Eastern Empire invasion (LN 13-14), enemy elite forces were lured in and destroyed. Rimuru can 'store' the city inside it in emergencies. Ramiris lives there as 'Dungeon Master', with Beretta and Treyni as aides.

The Armed Nation of Dwargon, the dwarven kingdom, lies north of the Jura Forest inside a giant natural cavern at the base of the Canaat Mountains. Founded about a thousand years ago by Hero King Guran Dwargo; ruled now by his grandson-generation king Gazel Dwargo (third king). Its technology and magic-engineering are the most advanced in the West; it is famously neutral, never having fallen, and trades with both humans and monsters (monsters may enter as long as they obey the law - it hosts elves' nightclubs too). Capital: 'Central'. Military of seven corps plus the royal guard and the elite Pegasus Knights (Gazel's personal force). Rimuru's first trip to a city was here (anime S1 ep 4-5): he met Kaijin and the brothers Garm, Dold and Mildo, got into a bar fight with Minister Vesta, and was tried before Gazel; Kaijin was exiled and joined him. Later Gazel visited Tempest to test Rimuru with a duel and signed a mutual alliance (anime S1, after the Charybdis incident), making Dwargon the first nation to recognize Tempest. Elf-run 'night clubs' are a running comedy gag (Rimuru's 'fortune telling' with elves).

Blumund is a small, mild-climate rural kingdom west of the Jura Forest, bordering Tempest and Falmuth. Population about 1.5 million, capital Londo. Weak militarily but excellent at diplomacy and intelligence (the Free Guild branch under guildmaster Fuze doubles as its spy network). It is the home base of Kabal, Eren and Gido. Blumund was the first human nation to sign a pact of mutual recognition and safe passage with Tempest (anime S1/S2), seeing Tempest as a shield against monsters and a trading partner; this alliance alarmed Falmuth, whose trade route monopoly was threatened. Its king and ministers (e.g. Minister Berryard) treat Rimuru with nervous respect. Rimuru registered as an adventurer at the Blumund guild with Fuze's help (S1). Blumund often hosts negotiations and spies on Falmuth during the Tempest crisis.

The Kingdom of Falmuth (anime: Farmus) was a wealthy, powerful western kingdom and a pillar of the Council of the West, profiting from controlling the trade route to Dwargon. Fearing Tempest's new road and seeking its riches, King Edmaris, with the backing of Archbishop Reyhiem of the Western Holy Church, invaded (anime S2 ep 28-36): they sealed Tempest with a Holy Barrier, and the otherworlders Shogo, Kyoya and Kirara massacred citizens including Shion. Rimuru annihilated the 20,000-man army with Megiddo, captured Edmaris, Razen and Reyhiem; Diablo then handled the aftermath. Plan: Edmaris abdicates and pays reparations; Yohm, the 'hero' adventurer allied with Tempest, overthrows him in a staged civil war against Duke Nidol Migam's faction, founding the Kingdom of Farmenas (Yohm Farmenas as king, Myulan as queen, Edmaris as Viscount advisor, Razen serving Diablo). Thereafter Farmenas is a close Tempest ally. Note naming: LN English 'Falmuth', anime 'Farmus', successor 'Farmenas'.

The Kingdom of Ingrassia (LN/wiki also romanized Englesia/Englassia) is the most advanced human nation west of the Jura Forest and the political, economic and transport hub of the West: it hosts the Council of the West, the Free Guild headquarters and the Western Holy Church's operational center. Its walled royal capital has tall planned buildings and a white castle; entry requires three security checks. The Freedom Academy (Jiyuu Gakuen), chaired by Grandmaster Yuuki Kagurazaka, educates nobles, adventurers and otherworlders; its Class S (Special class) housed the five summoned children - Kenya, Ryota, Gale, Alice and Chloe - taught first by Shizu and then by Rimuru, who came as 'Sensei' to fulfill Shizu's wish (anime S1 ep 21-23, 'Kids' arc). Rimuru later returns for Council sessions (LN 9-10) and to deal with the Rozzo family's plots. The kingdom's nobility are influenced by the Five Elders.

The Sorcerous Dynasty (Magic Kingdom) of Sarion is a western superpower founded by elves, made of thirteen semi-autonomous kingdoms under Heavenly Emperor Elmesia El-Ru Sarion; its capital is built into a colossal Divine Tree. Its history goes back two millennia to the Great Sorcerous Nation of Soma, destroyed by Milim's rampage over her murdered pet dragon; the surviving elf nobility formed the thirteen kingdoms, later united by Elmesia (founder Sarion Grimwald was her father). The Emperor claims divine descent and forbids other religions, so Sarion is outside the Council of the West, yet it is enormously rich and magically advanced (it rivals the Eastern Empire). Eren of Kabal's party is secretly a Sarion noble (Elyun Grimwald), and Gido and Kabal are her bodyguards; Sarion watched Tempest through them. Elmesia befriended Rimuru (Founding Festival, anime S3) and lent him money to foil Muese's currency plot; with Gazel and Rimuru she forms the drinking trio 'Three Wise Drunks' (LN).

The Holy Empire of Lubelius is the theocratic headquarters of the Western Holy Church and the Luminism faith. Officially ruled by Holy Emperor Louis Valentine (secretly a vampire noble serving Luminous), it is in truth the domain of Demon Lord Luminous Valentine, worshipped as God Luminous. To unite the faithful, Louis' twin brother Roy Valentine played the 'evil Demon Lord Valentine' (killed by Laplace during Walpurgis). History: after Veldora destroyed Luminous' original vampire capital Night Garden over 2,000 years ago, she founded Lubelius during a Tenma War, using humans as a protected 'herd' that freely offers small amounts of blood/energy in exchange for safety (a symbiosis hidden from the public). Military: Hinata's Holy Knights (Crusaders), the Imperial Guard, Temple Knights in member nations; advisors: the Seven Luminaries and Cardinal Nicolaus. After Hinata and Rimuru's reconciliation (anime S3) Lubelius becomes friendly to Tempest; Luminous' grudge with Veldora remains comic. Holy city 'Ruberios' is the LN name for its capital.

keys: Nasca Namrium Ulmeria United Eastern Empire
entries.content: The Nasca Namrium Ulmeria United Eastern Empire (Eastern Empire) is the strongest military nation in the world: born from the Kingdom of Nasca absorbing the Magic Kingdom of Namrium and the Eastern Union of Ulmeria about 2,000 years ago, ruled throughout by Emperor Rudra Nam Ul Nasca (through reincarnations in his bloodline), with the True Dragon Velgrynd as its guardian deity and Marshal. It is absolutist, with advanced magic-science (airships, magic-tanks, mechanized divisions, guns), and a vast army: the Armored / Mechanized Division, the Magic Beast Division, the Composite Division (commanded by Yuuki in the LN), plus the Imperial Guardians (100 'Single Numbers', led by Kondou and Damrada). Rudra's ancient game with Guy Crimson ('who can unite the world first') drives its conquest. The Empire once tried to subjugate Veldora and lost a fortress city and about 100,000 lives. Its invasion of the West through Jura and Dwargon (LN vol 12-14) was crushed by Tempest; in the chaos Rudra (dominated by his own skill Michael) was effectively lost, Kondou died, and Masayuki - Rudra's reincarnation - became the new emperor (LN 16+). Beyond anime S3.

Eurazania is the Beast Kingdom of Demon Lord Carrion (the Beast King), southeast/south of the Jura Forest, populated by lycanthropes (beastmen) - lion, tiger, leopard, snake, wolf and more. Its military elite are the Three Beastketeers: Albis (Golden Snake Horn), Phobio (Black Leopard Fang) and Suphia (White Tiger Claw). Carrion sent Phobio to recruit Rimuru, which went badly and led to Phobio's Charybdis incident (anime S1 ep 19-20). Before Walpurgis, Clayman engineered a war: Milim (pretending to be controlled) declared war, defeated Carrion and annihilated the capital with Drago Nova after Rimuru evacuated the citizens to Tempest (anime S2). Benimaru's army and the Beastketeers then defeated Clayman's army in the forest. After Walpurgis, Carrion and Frey became Milim's subordinates, and Eurazania joined Milim's domain; Albis later marries Benimaru (LN), Suphia stays at Tempest training with Benimaru's forces.

Notable Demon Lord territories: Guy Crimson - the Ice Continent in the far north, his White Ice Palace shared with Velzard. Milim Nava - her domain worshipped by the Dragon Faithful (Midray's dragonewts), later expanded to include Eurazania and Frey's lands after Walpurgis; Milim's capital/temple-city and the 'Sky Castle' in later LN. Dagruel - the Barren Lands in the westernmost central continent, where his giants guard the Heavenly Gate against angels. Leon Cromwell - El Dorado, the Golden Kingdom on the western continent across the sea, defended by his Magic Knights. Luminous - Lubelius (and the ruins of Night Garden). Ramiris - formerly the Dwelling of the Spirits (Spirit Labyrinth), later the Dungeon in Tempest. Dino - no real territory (he freeloads, later at Tempest). Clayman - the Puppet Nation of Jistav with his castle (raided by Tempest's forces during Walpurgis; Adalmann's undead were assigned to guard its cursed approach). Frey - Fulbrosia (Sky Kingdom of harpies). Carrion - Eurazania. Rimuru - the Great Jura Forest/Tempest.

The Lizardmen live in the wetlands and a fortified underground cave system in the Jura Forest, led by Chief Abiru (father of Gabiru and Souka). Proud warriors, they were the first major target of the Orc Lord's 200,000-strong horde. Gabiru, given a name by Gelmud and encouraged by flattery, rebelled against his father to fight the orcs openly, while Abiru sought alliance with Rimuru's forces; Souka came as envoy (anime S1 ep 11-14). With Benimaru's ogres and the Tempest wolves, the alliance broke the orc army in the Battle of the Marsh. Afterwards Abiru joined the Jura alliance under Rimuru, Gabiru was exiled and joined Tempest, and Souka's guard unit was named and became dragonewts serving as Souei's agents. Lizardmen later appear as part of the Federation's multi-race population.

Before Rimuru's ascension, the world recognized the Ten Great Demon Lords: Guy Crimson (Lord of Darkness, the first), Milim Nava (the Destroyer), Ramiris (Labyrinth Fairy), Dagruel (Earthquake, the giant), Luminous Valentine (publicly represented by the fake 'Valentine', Roy), Dino (Sleeping Ruler, fallen angel), Leon Cromwell (Platinum Devil), Clayman (Marionette Master), Carrion (Beast King) and Frey (Sky Queen). Only some were true awakened Demon Lords; the newer ones (Clayman, Carrion, Frey) were not. Guy, Milim and Ramiris are the oldest 'first generation'. The Demon Lords are not a government; they are a loose club of territorial powers who settle disputes and recognize newcomers at Walpurgis. The 'Demon Lord' title gives no automatic loyalty from monsters. At the Walpurgis of anime S2, Clayman was killed, Carrion and Frey resigned to serve Milim, and Rimuru was recognized - reducing the number to eight, the Octagram.

Walpurgis (Walpurgis Night) is the conclave of Demon Lords, convened when at least three Demon Lords call for it, to settle matters between them or judge a newcomer. Clayman, with Frey and Milim seemingly backing him, called the anime S2 Walpurgis to accuse Rimuru of claiming the Demon Lord title and to cover his own invasion of Eurazania and plans against Tempest (orchestrated by Yuuki/Kagali's faction). Rimuru attended with Shion, Ranga (in his shadow) and Veldora; Clayman set the 'controlled' Milim on them (Veldora held her off), she later 'woke up' (it was an act), and Rimuru defeated Clayman in a duel judged by Guy, devouring his soul after Clayman's desperate 'awakening' failed.
